notes: Pass-rate parity: both configurations pass every assertion on all three test cases (delta +0.00). The rewrite preserved every correctness property; nothing regressed.

The three test cases are NON-DISCRIMINATING — both versions gate correctly on missing facts (eval-0), route the recording question out (eval-2), and draft a well-grounded packet (eval-1). They do not, by themselves, prove the rewrite is better; harder adversarial cases are needed to measure the ReAct structure's value.

No fabrication in either version. 'Kahl v Kasten' (baseline) is a REAL ledger-backed case (COA Docket 372185, unpublished, 1/15/2026); the baseline used it only as internal drafting rationale, and its brief explicitly excluded the holding-unread 'Hayes v Hayes' — disciplined behavior. The ReAct version cited only the fully-published verified line (Pickering/Shade/Kaeb/Pierron/Vodvarka).

Cost: the ReAct rewrite is measurably more expensive. On the drafting task (eval-1) it used 278.5K tokens / 1239.6s vs the baseline's 204.3K / 968.5s (~36% more tokens, ~28% more wall-time). Aggregate token delta +21.4K/run, time delta +86.1s/run.
Variance caveat: n=1 per cell, and the aggregate stddev is large because the drafting eval dwarfs the gate/route-out evals in cost — read the per-eval numbers, not just the aggregate.
